summary: Initialized active v2 Bootstrap Planning Ledger for exact placeholder feature token `<feature name>`, registered it in ledger_registry.json, captured the collaborator planning persona and ledger-only constraints, and opened q-0001 to ask what we are working on before accepting product requirements.
Validated initial scaffold with `python3 scripts/pm-bootstrap-ledger-validate.py Plans/ledgers/v2/pldg-20260629-001-feature-name`; result pass with zero errors and zero warnings.

Jared named the feature `Free Models`, requested direct PM integration of `vava-nessa/free-coding-models` with substantial PM-specific modification, requested automatic upstream update intake because the maintainer continuously changes providers/settings, required all imported free models under one PM direct provider named `Free Models`, and required a GUI comment/link to the upstream GitHub repo.

Jared added that Free Models must monitor quota and usage similar to Multi-Account so PM can auto switch; provide a setting where the user chooses priority for the top 10 Free Models and PM automatically switches when a model is exhausted, rate limited, or otherwise ineligible; share logic from the Multi-Account switcher if already specced in Plans or address the gap if not; temporarily pull the upstream repo for deeper inspection; integrate natively rather than Docker; answer q-0002 as `Auto Apply`; answer q-0003 as adapting upstream runtime behavior such as schema normalizers, router scoring, fallback sets, probes, and update checks to PM; and answer q-0004 as every active free/free-limited model with badges.

Jared answered q-0005: Free Models priority should support per role/surface lists but also an option to set it globally, with global as the default to keep the GUI cleaner. Jared answered q-0006: use the Hybrid policy for prioritized models invalidated by Auto Apply, meaning PM should keep runtime continuity by promoting the next eligible model while preserving the invalidated user-prioritized slot visibly for review rather than silently erasing preference intent.

Jared clarified that the top 10 should be across all providers/models, not limited to the `Free Models` provider. Planning correction: the catalog still lists upstream free/free-limited models under one PM direct provider named `Free Models`, but the user-prioritized top-10 router/settings concept is PM-wide across all enabled providers/models, with Free Models entries participating alongside other provider/model entries.

Jared answered q-0008: paid-overage, metered API, costed, non-free, and credit-consuming models should be eligible for PM-wide top-10 automatic failover when their provider/model is enabled. Planning interpretation: PM does not require explicit per-entry opt-in before automatic routing may use a costed enabled entry, but must preserve cost/billing/credit badges, policy state, and Usage evidence so the route is visible and auditable.

Jared answered q-0009 with `Both`: PM should provide optional budget ceilings and notification thresholds for automatic failover into paid-overage, metered API, costed, or credit-consuming top-10 entries, and should also keep the always-on visibility path through badges, Usage records, and normal provider/account pressure state.

Jared answered q-0010: costed automatic failover budget/notification controls should default to presets while keeping levels configurable. The default preset thresholds are exactly `50`, `80`, `90`, `95`, and `100` percent of the configured budget.
Jared answered q-0011: Auto Apply upstream updates from `free-coding-models` should check on app launch plus a daily background check by default, and the cadence should be configurable.

Jared answered q-0012 with `the first option`: successful validated Auto Apply imports should use quiet notification/inbox summaries while blocking review is reserved for quarantined/unsafe changes. Jared also broadened refresh scope: model refresh should cover models from all providers, `inluding direct and cli(not just free)`, not just Free Models/free sources, and there should be a button near model settings that manually triggers the refresh.

Jared answered q-0013 with `the first`: manual/all-provider refresh should default to catalog/model metadata only. Planning interpretation: the default refresh path must not run live probes, health checks, quota checks, model calls, or other quota-spending/rate-limit-triggering checks; any deeper probe mode remains separate and must be explicit/configurable if later accepted.

Jared answered q-0014: `Yes auto apply, and Runtime behavior changes should be automatic too, but only for the free model provider.` Planning interpretation: validated upstream runtime behavior changes may auto-apply automatically only inside PM's single `Free Models` provider. This scoped exception does not extend to PM-wide direct providers, CLI-backed providers, or non-Free-Models refresh; those remain catalog/model metadata refresh by default unless separately specified.

Jared corrected the planning cadence: `Can you give me multiple questions at once instead of one at a time? This is taking too many turns.` Jared also answered q-0015: `You can make it all automatic for the free models. As long as it adapts to the PM structure.` Planning interpretation: automatic Free Models runtime behavior updates may include declarative descriptors and synthesized/code-level adapter behavior, but only when translated into PM-owned structure/contracts and validated there; raw upstream runtime behavior must not bypass PM adaptation.

Jared answered the batched q-0016 through q-0019 questions with `1. Yes 2. Yes 3. Yes 4. Yes`. Planning interpretation: PM should automatically roll back to previous known-good Free Models snapshots and quarantine bad automatic updates; Free Models Auto Apply should track upstream default branch/latest catalog by default with pinned-version/rollback controls; Free Models entries should reuse existing PM provider/account credentials and show setup-required badges/actions when missing; and models that stop being free/free-limited should leave the active Free Models list, remain available through their real provider/top-10 route if enabled, and preserve disabled/history state in Free Models.

Jared answered q-0020 through q-0023: `1. Yes 2. Yes 3. Yes 4. No`. Planning interpretation: PM should fall back outside the top 10 to the best eligible enabled model with a clear switch reason; the Free Models catalog should group by underlying provider with search/filter controls and visible badges; post-update verification should default to non-consuming structural/contract validation with live probes only in explicit configurable mode; and PM should not expose a technical Free Models update history/import-diff view to normal users because `this will be user facing`, users will not know how this works, and the target market is `users who are not developers and are just vibe coders`. The normal update surface must be plain-language and user-facing rather than developer/debug oriented.

Jared answered q-0024 through q-0027 with `1. Yes 2. Yes 3. Yes 4. Yes`. Planning interpretation: technical Free Models diagnostics should exist only behind Advanced/Support Diagnostics and stay hidden from the normal Free Models flow; Free Models should provide a simple guided connect/setup checklist for missing provider accounts or credentials using plain actions; quota/pressure/rate-limit states should use simple user-facing statuses such as Ready, Limited, Used up for now, Needs setup, May cost money, or Paused with raw technical details hidden unless expanded; and model-switch explanations should use plain reasons such as `that model is busy`, `used up for now`, or `needs setup`, with technical details only if expanded.

Jared answered q-0028 through q-0031 with `Yes to all 4`. Planning interpretation: PM should auto-suggest a starter global top-10 priority list based on currently best eligible models and make it easy to reorder; the Free Models catalog should be visible by default while routing only uses Ready/eligible/setup-complete entries; successful Free Models updates and non-critical status changes should stay quiet/plain-language by default while setup needed, cost risk, failed rollback, or quarantined unsafe updates interrupt the user; and PM should offer a simple `Use Free Models when possible` preset/toggle for non-developer users with advanced customization still available.

Jared answered q-0032 through q-0035: `1. Yes`; `2. No, by default paid providers should be preferred over the free models unless the user configured the free models above the paid ones in the top 10 list.`; `3. Yes`; and `4. Yes`. Planning interpretation: the `Use Free Models when possible` preset should be prominent but opt-in, not silently enabled by default; the rejected free-first preset wording is replaced by paid-provider-first default precedence unless the user's top-10 order places Free Models above paid providers; guided setup completion should rerun eligibility/catalog refresh and update starter top-10 suggestions; and the preset applies globally by default while respecting advanced per-role/surface overrides. Jared also added future onboarding/doctor sequencing context: `I need to redesign the onboarding and doctor setup next(not for you to do)`, and in that flow the user should setup paid providers first, then see Free Models and configure top 10 because paid providers will typically be preferred.

Jared answered q-0036 through q-0039 with `Yes to all 4`. Planning interpretation: newly imported and validated Free Models entries should appear automatically in the catalog and suggestions but must never silently reorder the user's saved top-10 list; automatic upstream runtime-behavior changes must become PM-owned adapter revisions that pass contract tests/quarantine with no raw upstream project code executed inside PM at runtime; Usage records/receipts for Free Models routes should show both the friendly `Free Models` provider and the underlying provider/model/account in plain expandable detail; and unsupported upstream-added provider/model entries should be shown as unavailable/needs app support rather than hidden or shown as ready.

Jared answered q-0040 through q-0043. q-0040: `1. Yes, however, there are configurable setting for different sections of PM, for example(but not limited to) the interviewer, auditor, assistant chat, etc. those configurable settings override the top 10 and the gui should state that. You should review the plans docs closely to see those different settings so you’re aware.` Planning interpretation: global/top-10 routing is primary only where no higher-precedence PM section/surface/role setting applies; existing PM configured settings such as interviewer, Auditor, Assistant Chat, Goal worker/verifier-adjudicator, Overseer/Worker/GUI-Frontend/High-Effort/Teacher and other scoped roles override global top-10, and the GUI must state that using requested/effective override grammar. q-0041 and q-0042 are yes. q-0043 is yes, but versioned Auto Apply snapshots are a debug/log artifact invisible to normal users unless they dive into Advanced/Support-style detail. Plans docs reviewed for section-setting awareness before updating ledger; no canonical Plans were edited.

Jared answered q-0044 through q-0047 with `Yes to all 4`. Planning interpretation: when a section-specific PM model setting is unavailable, exhausted, or blocked, PM should first fall back within that section/role policy and use global top-10 fallback only if that section allows it; section-specific model settings should allow users to select `Free Models` entries directly, subject to the same Ready/setup/quota/cost/underlying-provider attribution rules; pause/exclude should apply globally by default with Advanced controls for section-specific exceptions; and Auto Apply debug/log snapshots should use bounded retention, redact secrets/tokens/account identifiers by default, and be exportable only through Advanced/Support diagnostics.

Jared answered q-0048 through q-0051: `1. No you need to show the models, there is a massive difference in models.`; `2. There is no staging, PM just updates on the checks.`; `3. Yes`; `4. Yes`. Planning interpretation: section-specific Free Models settings must show actual model choices rather than a simple Free Models pool because model differences matter; Auto Apply should not have a separate staging concept and should update based on checks; paused/excluded entries remain visible under a Paused/Excluded filter with resume/re-enable controls; and normal Free Models UI should show a plain last checked/last updated summary plus action-needed statuses while detailed import-log/snapshot history stays in Advanced/Support diagnostics.

Jared answered q-0052 through q-0055 with `Yes to all` and challenged recommendation quality: `but how would you know the recommended ones?` Planning interpretation: section-specific Free Models selectors should show model-level badges/filters, keep incompatible or poor-fit models visible but disabled/labeled, keep the current known-good Free Models state active when Auto Apply checks fail while quarantining/logging the failed update without staging terminology, and sort/highlight `Recommended for this section` entries without hiding eligible manual choices. Recommendation must become an explicit PM-owned evidence/scoring question rather than an unsupported claim that PM magically knows the best model.

Jared challenged coding-strength inference and rejected recommendations for this version: `How would it know coding strength? You would need to look up reviews online. Or we will need to build a benchmark.` Jared then scoped the benchmark path out of the current project: `I think it would be better for me to build a benchmark outside of PM, run it and then load those results into PM code and have it pushed as an update. That is well outside the scope of this project though for now.` Final correction: `No to all, don’t do recommended models. I will address that in future versions of PM.` Planning interpretation: retire recommended-model sorting/highlighting, recommendation confidence/scoring/local learning/probe calibration, coding-strength claims, and starter/best-eligible suggestion language from the current Free Models scope; preserve future external benchmark/result-update concept as source-lineage only.

Jared answered the q-0060 through q-0063 batch with `1. That is a lot of info to display in a small area.` and `Ok`. Planning interpretation: current Free Models selectors should not cram every objective fact into a small row; objective model details need compact default presentation with progressive disclosure. Treat `Ok` as accepting the remaining current-scope clarifications: avoid `best eligible` starter recommendations for now, use deterministic eligibility/policy fallback rather than quality ranking, and keep future benchmark/review work outside current scope as source-lineage only.

Jared answered q-0064 through q-0067 with `yes to all 4`. Planning interpretation: collapsed Free Models model rows should show only model name, underlying provider, readiness/status, cost/free state, and a small capability icon group while moving context size, quota, setup, and other details into expand/hover/details; filters/search should expose fuller objective fields instead of rendering every field as a badge on every row; critical blockers such as Needs setup, May cost money, Used up for now, Paused, or Not supported here should always remain visible in collapsed rows; and neutral starter top-10 setup should begin as a guided editable template grouped by provider family/status rather than a quality-ranked recommendation list.

Jared answered q-0068 through q-0071 with `sounds good to all 4`. Planning interpretation: expanded model details should include upstream GitHub attribution/link, imported source/ref/version, underlying provider/account, setup steps, quota/pressure detail, cost/free caveats, and support/debug links while normal rows stay compact; disabled model rows should offer one primary plain action when possible; neutral starter top-10 templates should use deterministic buckets such as already configured paid providers, Ready Free Models, setup-needed Free Models, and enabled CLI/direct providers without implying quality order; and deterministic fallback should show a plain `why this switched` receipt with selected source layer, skipped entries, user/section policy, and visible reason while avoiding quality-score language.

Jared answered q-0072 through q-0075: `1. No notification`; `2. yes`; `3. If they arent supported, they just should show up at all`; `4. yes`. Planning interpretation: successful validated Free Models Auto Apply updates create no notification/inbox item; failed or quarantined updates show `Free Models update needs attention`, keep current known-good active, and offer Retry check plus View details; unsupported upstream additions should not appear in normal user surfaces at all; and manual model refresh near settings produces a unified all-provider summary while only Free Models Auto Apply can auto-apply Free Models runtime behavior changes.

Jared answered q-0076 through q-0079 with `yes to all`. Planning interpretation: saved top-10/section model slots that disappear or become ineligible should remain as `No longer available`, be skipped automatically, and ask for replacement only in settings/attention flows; unsupported upstream additions hidden from normal users still remain in Advanced/Support diagnostics/exports for source lineage and troubleshooting; successful no-notification Auto Apply updates show only `Last checked` and `Last updated` in normal settings with details behind expansion or Advanced/Support; and manual all-provider refresh uses plain per-provider statuses such as Updated, No changes, Needs sign-in, Skipped, or Failed.

Jared answered q-0080 through q-0083: `1. yes`; `2. yes`; `3. no, just update`; `4. yes`. Planning interpretation: Auto Apply accepts only the configured upstream source/channel with source hashes/PM schemas; imported models use stable PM IDs and alias/rename mappings; material upstream changes just update from checked Auto Apply results instead of preserving old saved choices disabled until separate safety review; and runtime behavior adaptation is limited to PM-owned declarative router/probe/normalizer/fallback config plus tests, rejecting upstream commands, proxies, telemetry hooks, credential writers, and arbitrary config writers unless a future explicit plan reopens them.

Jared answered q-0084 through q-0087 with `1. Yes`, `2. Yes`, `3. Yes`, `4. Yes`. Planning interpretation: checked material updates immediately control routing eligibility while preserving saved slots; newly imported supported Ready Free Models entries can enter deterministic outside-top-10 fallback immediately without mutating saved top-10; app-launch Auto Apply checks run after startup in the background using last known-good until complete; and manual all-provider refresh also triggers the Free Models Auto Apply check while non-Free-Models providers remain catalog/model-refresh-only.

Jared answered q-0088 through q-0091 with `Yes to all`. Planning interpretation: Free Models pressure state is keyed by underlying provider/account/model and shared with Multi-Account pressure while displayed under Free Models; unknown quota/reset signals use coarse pressure and conservative cooldowns with no fabricated percentages/reset times; fallback attempts per request are bounded by configurable global/section limits with plain stopped reasons; and partial streaming failures must show the partial/failure state with retry/switch action rather than silently retrying on a different model.

Jared answered q-0092 through q-0095 with `1. Yes 2. Yes. 3. Yes 4. Yes`. Planning interpretation: default bounded fallback limit is initial attempt plus 2 automatic fallback attempts per request, configurable globally and overrideable by section; attempt limit counts the initial selected/requested model plus every automatic switch attempt and resets only for explicit user retry or new request; cooldowned entries stay skipped until provider reset/cooldown expiry or explicit Retry now, with success clearing cooldown and failure extending pressure conservatively; and usage/fallback receipts include attempted models, skipped entries, and final selected/stopped result collapsed by default and expandable in details.

Jared answered q-0096 through q-0099 with `Yes to all`. Planning interpretation: offline/network failures during automatic background or launch checks keep last known-good active with only passive settings status unless manual refresh or repeated-failure threshold applies; Auto Apply/model refresh changes affect only new routing decisions after completion and never alter in-flight requests; manual all-provider refresh failures show per-provider plain statuses such as `Failed`, `Offline`, or `Needs sign-in`, keep existing catalogs active, offer Retry, and create no separate notifications; and Free Models setup delegates to the underlying PM provider/account setup flow, then returns to Free Models with eligibility refreshed instead of collecting credentials inside Free Models.

Jared answered q-0100 through q-0103 with `1. No setting.  The user can’t fix this.`, `2. Yes`, `3. Yes`, and `4. Yes`. Planning interpretation: repeated automatic background check failures must not expose a user-facing configurable threshold because the user cannot fix that failure class; in-flight requests record the exact model/provider snapshot they started with so later Auto Apply/model refresh changes cannot rewrite Usage/provenance; returning from underlying provider setup automatically reruns eligibility/catalog refresh for affected Free Models entries and updates `Ready`/`Needs setup` without changing saved top-10 order; and Free Models setup rows show the underlying provider name/account state before launching setup.

Jared answered q-0104 through q-0107 with `Yes to all`. Planning interpretation: repeated automatic Free Models check failures remain passive in normal UI and move only into Advanced/Support diagnostics unless routing availability is affected; normal Usage receipts show friendly model/provider names while exact snapshot IDs, source hashes, and upstream refs live in expanded details or Advanced/Support logs; additional Free Models entries that become Ready after provider setup are immediately eligible for deterministic outside-top-10 fallback without inserting into or reordering saved top-10; and setup rows use one plain primary action such as `Set up provider` or `Sign in`, preserve return context back to Free Models, and avoid import/runtime jargon in normal setup.

Jared answered q-0108 through q-0111 with `Yes to all`. Planning interpretation: routing-affecting Free Models check failures show a narrow normal UI state such as `Some Free Models are unavailable` on affected provider/entries while paid/direct providers continue normally rather than broad app-level warning; Usage/provenance preserves the friendly request-time name and shows later upstream rename/provider move only in expanded details; setup actions map plain labels by state (`Sign in`, `Set up provider`, `Reconnect`); and Advanced/Support diagnostics include last successful source/ref/hash, last failed check time, error class, affected provider/model IDs, and route impact with secrets/tokens always redacted.

Jared answered q-0112 through q-0115 with `Yes to all`. Planning interpretation: affected Free Models provider rows show a compact unavailable count and top plain reason with per-model details only after expand/filter/search; expanded details and Advanced/Support provenance show the alias/rename/provider-move chain from request-time snapshot to current catalog identity while normal Usage keeps the request-time friendly name; setup actions launch the exact underlying provider/account setup surface, preserve return target back to the originating Free Models row/list, and refresh eligibility on return even after navigating within provider settings; and Advanced/Support diagnostics offer redacted copy/export with redaction summary and never raw secret/token values.

Jared answered q-0116 through q-0119 with `Yes to all`. Planning interpretation: compact unavailable rows choose the top plain reason by priority (`Needs sign-in`, `Rate limited`, `Provider offline`, `No longer free`, `Update issue`, `Unknown`) and use `Multiple issues` when no single reason dominates; expanded per-model availability details include skip reason, underlying provider/account, last checked time, last successful route if known, cooldown/Retry now state if known, and source/ref while raw payloads remain Advanced/Support-only; setup cancel or failed auth returns to the originating Free Models row/list, preserves saved top-10, refreshes eligibility if possible, and shows plain status without notification; and the planning conversation stops generating feature-shaping questions and shifts to compile-readiness/open-gap scan before any canonical Plans compile request.
